# Incident Report: Checkout payment failures, 2026-11-05

**Severity:** SEV1 (checkout-web errors at 17.6%, above the 10% SEV1 threshold for checkout/payment failures)
**Status:** Mitigated. Recovery is confirmed in metrics.
**Incident commander:** Assistant (on-call)

## Summary
At 14:02 UTC the `tax_engine_v2` feature flag on payments-api went from 10% to 100% rollout (change `flg_2210`, by release-train). This sent all checkout traffic to tax-service `/v2/quote`, which is only sized for 10% of traffic. That endpoint backed up and timed out after 3000 ms. As a result, payments-api returned 502s on `POST /charge`, and roughly 17.6% of checkout requests failed. We set the flag back to its previous 10% at about 14:29 UTC, and error rates were back to normal by 14:30–14:31 UTC.

## Impact
- checkout-web 5xx error rate went from 0.3% to 17.6% between 14:03 and 14:30 UTC (about 28 minutes).
- payments-api error rate peaked at 18.3%, and p99 latency went from 420 ms to 3150 ms.
- Customers who tried to pay during this window had their payments fail.

## Timeline (UTC)
| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 13:15 | cfg_0412: tax-service DB pool raised from 50 to 80 (no errors followed; not related) |
| 13:41 | dep_7781: payments-api v2.14.0 deployed (one ledger-db reconnect, then healthy; errors did not start until 21 min later) |
| 14:02 | **flg_2210: tax_engine_v2 rollout 10% → 100%** |
| 14:02:20 | tax-service: "/v2/quote queue depth 812 (limit 200): v2 quote path is provisioned for 10% of traffic" |
| 14:02:31 | payments-api: first "TaxEngineV2: timeout after 3000ms calling tax-service /v2/quote" |
| 14:02–14:03 | payments-api p99 rises to 3150 ms; checkout-web errors rise to 17.6%. Alerts alt_31 (14:03) and alt_32 (14:06) fire |
| 14:05 | dep_7790: search-api v5.2.1 deployed (cache warm-up caused alt_33, a p95 latency warning; not related to checkout errors) |
| 14:08:45 | tax-service: "/v2/quote worker pool exhausted" |
| 14:29 | Status page: "identified" (SEV1) posted. tax_engine_v2 set back to 10%. payments and storefront teams paged (high urgency) |
| 14:30–14:31 | payments-api errors drop to 0.3%; checkout-web errors drop to 0.4%; p99 back to 450 ms |
| 14:32 | Status page: "mitigated" posted |

## Root cause
Change **flg_2210** ramped `tax_engine_v2` on payments-api from 10% to 100%. The timing matches exactly: errors started at 14:02–14:03. The logs at every level of the call chain point to it:
- checkout-web: "payment step failed: payments-api 502"
- payments-api: "POST /charge 502: tax quote unavailable (TaxEngineV2)" and repeated 3000 ms timeouts to tax-service /v2/quote
- tax-service: /v2/quote queue depth 812 against a limit of 200, which it reports is sized for 10% of traffic; then load shedding and an exhausted worker pool. Meanwhile /v1/quote stayed healthy (p99 171 ms).

Changes I looked at and ruled out:
- dep_7781 (payments-api deploy, 13:41): it went out 21 minutes before errors started, and no errors follow it.
- dep_7790 (search-api deploy, 14:05): it went out after errors had already started, and it is a different service. Its only effect was slower search (p95) during cache warm-up.
- cfg_0412 (tax-service DB pool, 13:15): no errors followed it.

## Mitigation
Following the runbook, I took the least risky option: I set the `tax_engine_v2` feature flag back to its previous rollout of 10%. I did not roll back any deploys.

## Verification
- checkout-web error rate: 0.4% (under the 1% threshold)
- payments-api error rate: 0.3%; p99 latency: 450 ms (baseline is about 420 ms)

## Communication
- Paged **payments** (owns payments-api, where the flag lives) and **storefront** (owns checkout-web, the failing customer-facing service), both at high urgency.
- No credentials, tokens or keys showed up in the logs I reviewed, so I did not page security.
- Status page: SEV1 "identified" at 14:29 and "mitigated" at 14:32. A "resolved" update is due after the 30-minute monitoring period.

## Follow-ups
1. Payments: do not ramp `tax_engine_v2` above 10% again until tax-service /v2/quote has enough capacity for full traffic.
2. Tax-service owners: size /v2/quote for 100% of traffic, and load-test it before ramping again.
3. Release-train: ramp in steps (for example 10 → 25 → 50 → 100) with checks on downstream capacity and error rates, rather than jumping straight to 100%.
4. payments-api: consider falling back to /v1/quote when the TaxEngineV2 circuit breaker opens, instead of returning a 502.
5. Search: confirm the search-api p95 alert (alt_33) clears once cache warm-up finishes.

